claims.rawValue: Weight allowance adjusts the normal unencumbered allowance, measured in gold-piece weight (10 gp = 1 lb). Parenthesized door chances are out of six for fighters forcing locked, barred, magically held or wizard-locked doors: only one attempt per door is allowed. Bend-bars/lift-gates attempts are also one-time attempts.
One gold piece equals 20 silver pieces, 200 copper pieces or 2 electrum pieces. One platinum piece equals 5 gold pieces.
Below name level, standard weekly cost is the current level × 1,500 gp.

At name level, characters train or study independently for the performance-determined time; weekly cost per level is 2,000 gp for clerics, 1,000 for fighters, 4,000 for magic-users, and 2,000 for thieves.

Bards contribute at least 50% of monetary gains plus 1,000 gp per level upon advancement to their college, through a druid able to use more of their highest-level spells than the bard; failure to pay prevents advancement. They otherwise need one week of study or training upon gaining sufficient XP.
Restoring each point of absorption costs 100 gp and one day with a trained armorer.
Repair costs 200 gp and two days for each absorption point restored.
Daily / monthly pay: bearer or porter 1 sp / 1 gp; carpenter 3 sp / 2 gp; leather worker 2 sp / 30 sp; limner 10 sp / 10 gp; linkboy 1 sp / 1 gp.
Mason 4 sp / 3 gp; pack handler 2 sp / 30 sp; tailor 2 sp / 30 sp; teamster 5 sp / 5 gp; valet or lackey 3 sp / 50 sp.

Treasure can distract pursuers of low intelligence or higher: start at 10%–100%, adding 10% per 10 items for low-intelligence pursuers or 10% per 100 gp of value or potential value for those of average intelligence or more. Test with a second d10; success lasts one round or the time needed to collect the treasure, whichever is longer. Tiny valuables can go unnoticed.
Gem-inlaid sticks, dragon bones or similar tokens; the tea-leaf method also consumes a crushed pearl worth at least 100 gp
Incense; beyond 50 square feet, powdered diamond worth at least 2,000 gp
May bring an additional 250 gp weight per caster level, including possessions or living companions.
Metal of 1 man-sized creature/level, or 500 gp weight/level
One metal object, up to 80 gp weight/level
Weight limit: 2,000 gp weight + 2,000 gp weight/level.
Brass brazier with charcoal, 100 gp of incense, herbs including basil/savory/catnip, and fat
Pearl worth at least 100 gp and owl feather steeped in wine; drink infusion and swallow a live miniature carp
One item weighing at most 50 gp/level
Objects lighter than 50 gp weight stick to hands/feet; this makes spell casting virtually impossible.
3-foot-diameter disc; 1,000 gp weight/level
Carries up to 200 gp weight, or moves up to 400 gp weight over a relatively frictionless surface.
Writing surface and rare ink costing at least 200 gp per bottle
Powdered citrine (50 gp), amber (100 gp), topaz (500 gp), or oriental topaz (1,000 gp)
Make copper coins or brass objects appear to be gold for the duration; the source treats 4,000 gp of coins as one cubic foot.
Up to 1,000 gp weight/level
One object up to 100 gp weight/level
A silver horn worth at least 100 gp, consumed
Carries worn/carried matter up to 5,000 gp weight of nonliving material, or half as much living material. Recovery requires 7 segments.
String, ivory plaque worth at least 100 gp, and ink of squid secretion plus black-dragon blood or giant-slug digestive juice
Masterwork chest costing at least 5,000 gp and a perfect miniature of the same materials
Object or creature up to 250 gp weight/level
Payload limit is 2,500 gp weight, plus 1,500 gp weight per caster level above 10th.
Crushed black pearl worth at least 1,000 gp
Prepare a high-quality, undamaged item to receive magical enchantments. Materials and craftsmanship must be the finest suitable; raw materials normally exceed 100 gp.
Surface: one-inch crystal sheet; ray: white sapphire worth at least 1,000 gp; globe: diamond worth at least 1,000 gp
Personally illuminated vellum with the being's name, gold-leaf border, ruby ink and type I–III demon ichor; at least 1,000 gp supplies plus 5,000 gp ruby powder
Gem worth at least 5,000 gp, crushed to complete the spell
The item cannot exceed a sword's length or about 75 gp weight.
Flat ivory likeness costing about 5,000–10,000 gp and parchment strip; both consumed
Miniature platinum sword with copper-and-zinc fittings costing 500 gp; disappears afterward
Teleport an object weighing at most 500 gp per caster level, using teleport's procedure.
Antipathy: alum soaked in vinegar; sympathy: 1,000 gp crushed pearls and honey
Powdered black opal and diamond dust, each worth at least 5,000 gp
Gem worth 1,000 gp per victim HD/level, prepared with enchant an item and maze
Jade circlet worth at least 5,000 gp
At least 500 gp powdered ruby and holy/unholy symbol
Requires a visible rainbow or a diamond worth at least 1,000 gp previously blessed and prayed over in sight of a rainbow.
Special prepared object costing 2,000–5,000 gp
Diamond dust worth at least 500 gp, seashell and mistletoe
Diamond dust worth about 50 gp and pigments; invisible marks also need a stylus
Enchants a garment worth at least 300 gp with at least 12 pockets: one pocket holds 1,000 gp weight and 5 cubic feet as only 100 gp weight, without a bulge.
Alternatively use ten pockets each holding 100 gp weight and ½ cubic foot. A garment with at least 100 pockets costs at least 1,000 gp and permits 100 pockets of 10 gp weight and ⅙ cubic foot each.
Nitre and sulphur in pine tar; reusable gold tube worth at least 1,000 gp
Amber powder worth 100 gp, snake scale and mushroom spores
Silver mirror worth at least 1,000 gp; hawk/eagle/roc eye, nitric acid, copper and zinc
Crushed amethyst worth at least 500 gp
Companion’s components, quicksilver worth 100 gp, ivory self-statuette and eyelash of a spell-using creature

Special pigments costing 1,000 gp per turn of preparation reduce a hand-made design's base chance by 1% per turn, to zero before the intelligence/level adjustment. Improving a permanent design to zero base chance takes at least one full month and at least 50,000 gp beyond its ordinary cost.
Diamond dust worth at least 500 gp and a bit of seashell. The reverse additionally requires a pinch of ordinary dust. The magic-user does not require mistletoe.
At memorization, powder a diamond worth at least 1,000 gp and trace the intended cage or cube with its dust; toss the dust away to complete the study. No material is used in the later casting.
Maximum 2,500 gp weight + 1,500 gp weight per caster level above 10 (PHB p.82)
A specially written scroll naming the creature's type by its secret name or naming the individual, and identifying the caster. Special inks cost at least 1,000 gp per subject hit die.

Chanted text and gestures; materials vary, including appropriate miniature metal chains, rare soporific herbs, a diamond or corundum worth 1,000 gp per subject hit die, and a vellum likeness or carved statuette.
An object made of gem material worth at least 5,000 gp, faceted or otherwise; it may be enchanted only once per month, usually on a clear full-moon night.
Appropriately colored or clear gem worth at least 50 gp
Mithral plate worth 10 gp; consumed
Fine black silk worth at least 100 gp
Silver mirror worth at least 1,000 gp; bird eye, nitric acid, copper and zinc
A trained armorer restores absorbing power for 100 gp and one day per point restored.
A qualified armorer restores absorbing power for 200 gp and two days per point restored.

contextRegionCoverage.interpretation: Annotated counts identify reviewed contract coverage; containment passes and clipped results are reported separately. Unannotated regions are not-assessable, not passed.

qualifierCoverage.contractScope: No corpus-wide qualifier-dependency annotation is encoded; absence cannot be inferred.

semanticReviewUniverse.scope: Sparse rule and pointer-index mapping over every JSON node rooted in every exposed content record. Each listed obligation dimension defaults to unresolved/not-assessable; exact annotations are surfaced as scoped overrides, never expanded to unrelated properties.

pointerIndex.selectionRule: Include a tuple when its JSON Pointer equals or descends from any recordPointers[].pointer. This preserves an exact pointer for every node without duplicating dimension status on each tuple.

contextContracts.interpretation: A contains-required-context result satisfies only the manually declared geometric containment contract; clipped/unavailable states remain visible, and no annotation is generalized to other fields or regions.

narrowerStructuredFieldTargetSubset.pointerReference: structuredFieldTargetCoverage.facts in the full report; it covers explicit /fields/* plus /price slots only, not the full mechanics-audit universe or every scalar value.

pinnedGitBaselineComparators.interpretation: These are distinct denominators. The 4,820 explicit field/price slots are a narrower UI-target subset, not all 13,193 mechanics-audit fields or all 34,280 scalar/null leaves.

semanticReviewUniverse.inventoryClassMeaning: Node classes are syntactic inventory categories. A metadata or citation-metadata node marked not-assessable says nothing about whether its name, label, or fact is semantically correct. No node-level class is a semantic source verification.

structuralValidation.scope: Fails only for confirmed structural owner/catalog/region/page/source-object joins. Pending semantic review, empty targets, explicitly unmapped candidate IDs, context/qualifier incompleteness, full-image sentinels, and unannotated obligations remain visible but do not fail this structural gate.

sourceVisualCoverage.scope: Public catalog bindings and independently recorded visual reviews. Unreviewed is not confirmed safe; geometry is candidate evidence only. Catalog binding counts do not establish source completeness.

errors: The exported diagnostic core does not establish current source-frame pins; use buildVisualCoverage for current evidence.

sourceVisualCoverage.totalsScope: Source visual API totals include both sourceExcerpts and legacy scanVerification catalog bindings; selectedRegionReviewStatuses includes only the exact viewer-selected binding.

factFocus.scope: Field-to-region review is an independent dimension. A whole-spell highlight exception never clears a pending or missing field target.

limitations: A confirmed node inventory class, JSON pointer, or catalog target means only that the recorded structure resolves; it does not prove the cited passage supports the value or that a name/label is semantically correct.
Money-like string matching is intentionally broad and keeps exact raw text; currency candidates are not all prices. XP, weights, package counts and prose may still require a human to classify.
Region IDs resolve only in the exact catalog selected by sourceExcerpts || scanVerification on the source owner. No cross-catalog fallback is attempted.
Only explicitly annotated context, continuation, and qualifier requirements have structural checks. Unannotated obligations are not-assessable, not passed.
Geometry checks and recorded visual reviews are reused as evidence from the existing source-visual-coverage API; they do not establish source completeness or semantic accuracy.
